title: Composite Anomaly Fusion and Triage Runbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This runbook defines a cross-signal anomaly fusion and operator triage workflow for platform engineers handling multi-signal degradations that impact LLM inference quality, latency, and cost. The goal is to reduce mean time to actionable insight (MTTAI) by correlating signals from telemetry, model outputs, and customer-reported anomalies into a single playbook run. Use this when an alert or dashboard shows a sustained degradation across two or more orthogonal signals (examples in Scope).

Scope and when to use this runbook
---------------------------------
Use this runbook when any of the following conditions hold for > 5 minutes: 
- Simultaneous token-latency percentile increases (P95 or P99) and spike in model retry/error rate.
- Degraded model quality signals (e.g., eval drift or automated scoring) coincident with increased prompt truncation or token length variance.
- Cost-per-inference rising while throughput or success rate drops (possible batching/cache degradation).

This runbook is NOT intended for single-signal transient blips (use normal alert flow) or for explicit capacity incidents called out by the autoscaler.

Owners and roles
----------------
- Primary oncall (platform operator): first responder for triage and containment.
- Model runtime lead (runtime team): investigates kernel/quantization/runtime regressions.
- Observability lead (telemetry team): validates signal integrity and alerting logic.
- Customer-facing engineer (CSE): coordinates customer communication if a tenant is impacted.
- Incident commander (IC): for escalations beyond 30 minutes or if SLA breach is imminent.

SLOs and thresholds referenced in this doc
-----------------------------------------
| Signal | Baseline / SLO | Triage threshold (alert) | Critical threshold (escalate) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| P95 token latency (region) | < 300ms | > 400ms sustained 5m | > 600ms sustained 5m |
| Error rate (generation 5xx/timeout) | < 0.2% | > 1% sustained 5m | > 3% sustained 5m |
| Eval-quality score (regression) | delta <= 0.5 pt | delta >= 1.5 pt | delta >= 3.0 pt |
| Token cost per inference | <= baseline +10% | > baseline +20% | > baseline +40% |

Signals to collect immediately (quick checklist)
------------------------------------------------
- Metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency (region/model variant), error rates, request rate (rps), tokens per request, batching size distribution.
- Logs: recent runtime warnings/errors, kernel switch traces, GPU OOM or MIG events.
- Traces: end-to-end traces for 3–5 sample failed or slow requests.
- Model outputs: recent generation outputs for automated eval scoring (sample 50 requests evenly across tenants).
- Telemetry health: verify exporters, ingestion lag, sampling rates, and metric cardinality changes.
- Customer signals: support tickets, dashboards from customer tenants, and synthetic customers.

Immediate containment (first 10 minutes)
---------------------------------------
1) Announce on #platform-incident channel with short context: affected region, models, estimated impact (SLO type). Example: 
   "INCIDENT: Composite anomaly: region-us-west, models gpt-open-8q & re-ranker 2. Affected: P95 latency +150ms, error rate 1.7%. Primary oncall Maya taking triage."
2) Pull 1–2 sample traces and model outputs into the incident thread.
3) Air-gap suspect traffic slices: reduce routing weight to non-critical regions/models or activate canary fallback model variant (see Fallback matrix below) to limit blast radius.
4) If token-cost spike is present, enable token-capping policy for noisy tenants (operator CLI step below).

Structured triage procedure (step-by-step)
------------------------------------------
Step 1 — Signal integrity validation (5–10m)
- Confirm that affected signals are not ingestion/aggregation artifacts.
- Run the telemetry health checklist: aggregator lag (< 20s), time window alignment, no schema changes in last 15m.
- Quick commands: 
```bash
# Check prometheus remote write lag
kubectl -n telemetry exec -it prometheus-0 -- curl -sS localhost:9090/api/v1/status/runtimeinfo | jq .
# Verify trace ingestion delay in trace-service
kubectl -n observability logs deployment/trace-processor | tail -n 200 | grep "ingest-delay"
```
If telemetry is stale, escalate to Observability lead and mark this a telemetry-integrity incident.

Step 2 — Narrow by dimension (10–20m)
- Slice by region, model-variant, tenant, and request pathway (streaming vs batch).
- Queries to run (PromQL examples):
  - P95 latency by model: 
    sum by(model) (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(response_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)))
  - Error rate by cluster: 
    sum by(cluster) (rate(request_errors_total[5m])) / sum by(cluster) (rate(requests_total[5m]))
- Identify the smallest dimension where the degradation is concentrated. If multi-region, prefer regional containment.

Step 3 — Check runtime and resource signals (10–20m)
- Verify GPU health (temperature, preemption, MIG eviction), kernel switches, and quantization fallback logs.
- Check node-level metrics: CPU steal, memory pressure, network egress saturation.
- Common commands: 
```bash
# GPU health summary
kubectl -n runtime exec -it gpu-monitor-0 -- /usr/local/bin/gpu-summary.sh --since 30m
# Node pressures
kubectl top nodes | sort -k3 -n
```
If node-level resource events align with the incident, follow the GPU pool maintenance runbook (link in related_pages).

Step 4 — Model and prompt-level investigation (20–40m)
- Pull 50 recent model outputs across the affected variant and run automated eval scoring. Compare with baseline prompt set.
- Check for recent model version changes or rollout events in the last 24h.
- If prompt truncation or token-length variance is elevated, inspect client SDK change logs (e.g., updated tokenizer behavior).

Step 5 — Containment and mitigations (parallel)
Possible operator actions (choose one or more depending on root cause):
- Route traffic to a compatible fallback model variant (canary or older quantization profile).
- Reduce batching window to lower latency for interactive tenants. Command example: 
```bash
# Reduce batching target for model `gpt-open-8q`
redwoodctl runtime config set --model gpt-open-8q --batch-target-ms 15
```
- Enable read-only prefix cache (fast path) if KV cache consistency suspected.
- Roll back a recent kernel/driver change (follow kernel rollback operator script).
- Throttle noisy tenants with token caps: 
```bash
redwoodctl tenant throttle set --tenant-id tenant-123 --token-cap 50000 --duration 2h
```

Escalation matrix
------------------
- If critical thresholds breached (see table) or incident > 30m: IC + runtime lead join.
- If the incident affects > 10% of revenue-bearing tenants or any enterprise with an active contract: notify Sales Engineering and Customer Success within 30 minutes.
- If evidence of data corruption, security breach, or kernel panic: tag Security and open a restricted channel.

Fallback matrix (quick reference)
---------------------------------
- Latency spike + no model-quality regression: preferentially route to fallback lower-latency quantized variant.
- Quality regression + stable latency: route to prior model version (pinned stable) and freeze rollouts.
- Both latency and quality regress: isolate by tenant and enable emergency throttles; consider partial rollback of runtime change.

Dashboard and alerting adjustments (post-containment)
----------------------------------------------------
- Add a composite panel that shows correlated time-series: P95 latency, error rate, eval-delta, token-cost across the same time axis.
- Create a derived SLI that triggers only when two signals cross thresholds within 5m to reduce noise (alert policy example below).

Example alert rule (YAML)
------------------------
```yaml
alert: CompositeAnomalyFusion
expr: |
  ( (sum by(region)(rate(request_errors_total[5m])) / sum by(region)(rate(requests_total[5m]))) > 0.01 )
  and (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(response_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region)) > 0.4)
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Composite anomaly: errors + latency in {{ $labels.region }}"
```

Post-incident actions and templates
----------------------------------
- Within 24 hours: owner submits incident timeline and root-cause hypothesis to the incident tracker.
- Within 72 hours: schedule a blameless retrospective if the incident met any of these triggers: SLA breach, customer impact > 2 tenants, or remediation required in multiple teams.
- Retrospective template fields: incident summary, timeline (5-min buckets), contributing factors, actions (owner + due date), verification plan.

Verification and closure criteria
--------------------------------
- Telemetry indicates return to baseline for 3x the incident duration or 24 hours (whichever is longer).
- All mitigation toggles (fallback routing, throttles) are reverted or replaced with stable configs.
- Postmortem draft exists and has at least two reviewers from different teams.

Appendix: quick command references and useful queries
----------------------------------------------------
- List active model rollouts: `redwoodctl rollout list --status active`
- Show last 24h kernel switches for a model: `kubectl -n runtime logs daemonset/runtime-kernel --since=24h | grep gpt-open-8q`
- PromQL: token cost per inference: `sum by(model) (rate(token_cost_total[5m]) / rate(requests_total[5m]))`
